speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you're experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To understand what is happening, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD). The rapid onset of myoclonus or akinetic mutism is not yet described, but the combination of rapidly progressive dementia, early gait ataxia, and specific psychiatric changes in a 44-year-old is highly suggestive of sporadic CJD. I am requesting an MRI of the brain to look for cortical ribboning and the basal ganglia signal changes characteristic of this condition. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain
